# Adversarial review: the file-editing API ## Recommendation The five statuses should not be one mutually exclusive value. The sequences you asked about show at least four separate facts, and each has its own lifetime: | Fact | What it describes | Lifetime | |---|---|---| | `dirty` | Whether another write is needed before storage holds `text` | Changes with each revision and each write that lands | | `saving` | Whether a guarded write is in flight. It may be carrying older text. | One attempt | | `failure` | The latest finished attempt was refused, for example because storage is offline or a permission was denied. | Until a write lands, or the input is reverted to match storage | | `conflict` | Storage no longer matches the witness the input was based on. | Until it is explicitly resolved | These facts occur together in normal use: dirty while saving, dirty while in conflict, saving while a failure is still showing. A single `status` turns them into a display priority, so callers lose real information. Your hypothesis holds: a status earns its place when its values exclude each other. Two parts of the status do meet that test. One is how the file can be opened (`loading | missing | not-text | ready`); that moves into acquisition. The other is the kind of save problem, which `failure` and `conflict` payloads already distinguish. **What I recommend:** acquire the editor asynchronously, keep one folder-owned editor per path, and expose a flat snapshot of those independent facts. Write operations return Results; they don't record refusals in shared state. ## What the snapshot implements today The nested proposal is already implemented here: `BufferSnapshot` holds `ready` with `text` and an optional `unsaved` (`packages/folder/src/edit-owner.ts:141-145`). I could only read this frozen snapshot, not the live main conversation. The code already tracks the distinctions above internally, but the public union hides them: - **Typing during a save keeps showing `saving`.** New input inherits `saving: input?.pending.saving` (`edit-owner.ts:1152`). So `saving` already means "an attempt for some revision is running", not "the current text is being saved". - **Failures and conflicts already have different lifetimes.** New typing clears a failure but keeps a conflict (`edit-owner.ts:1153-1156`). A failure on an older revision is dropped, and the newer revision is sent at once (`edit-owner.ts:860, 871-872`). - **Typing after a conflict re-runs a write that must fail.** Each typing pause schedules a save (`edit-owner.ts:1162`). The loop then clears the error and marks the input as saving (`edit-owner.ts:847`), and it sends against the same stale `from`, which conflicts again. The status goes conflict → saving → conflict. In `FileEditor.svelte:81-91`, the conflict alert disappears while "Saving…" shows. - **A clean buffer loses its text when the file is deleted elsewhere.** With `doc === null` and no input, `shownText` is undefined and the status becomes `unavailable` (`edit-owner.ts:1093-1099, 575-590`). `FileEditor.svelte:54-64` works around this by keeping a `lastShown` copy, so the current contract doesn't meet that caller's need. - **`save()` can report a later revision's failure.** Calling `save()` while a save is running joins the drain loop (`edit-owner.ts:806-808`), which returns the outcome of its last attempt. Suppose revision r1 lands, typing creates r2, a timer joins it, and r2 fails. The caller who asked to save r1 gets an error even though r1 was stored. - **Reading a getter starts a file read, so callers avoid the getter.** The Svelte adapter reads the file when `buffer` is accessed in the `unread` state (`packages/svelte/src/edits.ts:24-27`). Honeycrisp and Whispering only touch `buffer` when `file.data?.kind === 'text' || isWriting || isUnsaved` (`FileDetail.svelte:77-80`, `RecordingDetail.svelte:74-76`). - **`buffer.error` mixes unrelated kinds of error.** It combines read errors, refusals, missing or non-text source, and save errors. Keeping it accurate takes the refusal bookkeeping in `record`, `execute` and `refusalOf` (`edit-owner.ts:504-563`). - **The folder-level names are confused.** `isUnsaved` means "has a failure", and `isSaving` means "unsaved and not failed" (`whispering.svelte.ts:1039-1049`). ## Definitions - **Revision:** each accepted `replaceText` or `change` increments it. - **Witness:** the exact stored content the input was based on. It is updated whenever a write lands or a clean editor refreshes. - **Saved(r):** storage is confirmed to hold revision r, or a later revision, through a guarded write. - **Dirty:** another write is needed before storage holds `text`. It is false when `text` equals the witness and nothing is in flight, or when `text` equals the in-flight text. - **Save (attempt):** one guarded write of the current text against the witness. - **Flush:** resolves when the revision that was current at the call is saved, including when a later saved revision supersedes it. It never reports on revisions accepted after the call. It fails with the failure or conflict that blocks that revision. - **Durability:** separate from all of the above. Text held in memory is not crash recovery. ## Sequences 1. **Typing during a save.** r1 is in flight and r2 is accepted, so `saving` and `dirty` are both true. When r1 lands, the witness becomes r1 and `dirty` stays true, so autosave sends r2. `flush()` called at r1 resolves `{revision: 1}`. 2. **Reverting while a save runs.** The editor holds witness W and r1 is in flight. A revert is an ordinary edit back to W's text, so `dirty` is true: r1 will land, and W must then be written back. Nothing is refused, and no `discard` lock is needed. This is how the current code behaves (`edit-owner.ts:1139-1147`), but the new definition makes it visible to callers. 3. **Retrying a failure.** The retry keeps the failure visible: `failure` is set and `saving` is true, so the UI can show "Not saved: offline · retrying…". The failure clears only when a write lands. Typing does not clear it either; the next autosave is simply another retry. This is the main product choice: it removes the flicker and contradicts the premise that a failure and a running retry exclude each other. The current behaviour, where typing makes the failure disappear, is the alternative. 4. **Typing after a conflict.** The conflict stays, input is accepted, and autosave pauses because a guarded write against the same witness cannot succeed. Autosave starts again in two cases. One is `resolve(...)`. The other is a refresh showing that storage equals the witness again, which clears the conflict. 5. **A refresh fails while text is usable.** `storage.error` is set, while `text`, `dirty` and autosave are unchanged; writes stay guarded. 6. **A refresh finds the file deleted, with no input.** The editor keeps `text` as the last known content and sets `storage.state` to `'missing'`. Typing is accepted. The first save, or an eager refresh check, turns this into a `conflict` with `current: null`. Only `resolve('mine')` recreates the file. The `lastShown` workaround is no longer needed. 7. **A refresh finds the file deleted, with input.** This is an eager conflict with `current: null`, and autosave pauses. ## Greenfield API ```ts type Editor = { readonly path: string; readonly state: { text: string; // always present revision: number; dirty: boolean; saving: boolean; failure?: SaveFailure; // latest finished attempt was refused conflict?: SaveConflict; // carries the observed `current` storage: { state: 'present' | 'missing' | 'not-text'; error?: ReadError }; }; readonly locked?: string; // an exclusive action holds the path markdown(schema?: S): MarkdownContent; replaceText(text: string): Result; change(c: DocumentChange): Result; revert(): void; // text := witness text, as an ordinary edit flush(): Promise>; resolve(choice: 'mine' | 'theirs' | { text: string }): Promise>; subscribe(fn: () => void): () => void; release(): void; // decrements the count of holders }; folder.open(path, schema?): Promise, OpenError /* missing | not-text | read */>>; ``` Vanilla use: ```ts const opened = await folder.open('notes/a.md'); if (opened.error) return report(opened.error); const editor = opened.data; const stop = editor.subscribe(render); editor.replaceText(editor.state.text + '\nMore.'); const done = await editor.flush(); // { revision } covering this edit, or the blocking problem stop(); editor.release(); // held input stays with the folder until saved or closed ``` Svelte. The parent owns loading: ```svelte {#await folder.open(path)} {:then opened} {#if opened.error} {:else}{/if} {/await} ``` ```svelte {#if s.conflict}Changed elsewhere {:else if s.failure}Not saved: {s.failure.message}{#if s.saving} · retrying…{/if} {:else if s.dirty || s.saving}Saving… {:else if s.storage.state === 'missing'}Deleted elsewhere {:else}Saved{/if} {#if s.conflict} {:else if s.failure} {/if} {#if s.storage.error}

{s.storage.error.message}

{/if}
